title: PI plan — tranche 7 (retrospective, 2026-11-28)
body:
# PI plan — tranche 7

## Objectives

O1 S16's inference ledger and prompt audit are accepted: every model call the conveyor makes is a durable, tenant-scoped row carrying the prompt's identity, the token counts and both prompt-cache classes, so cost and cache are a query. O2 S06c's MCP tasks surface is accepted: one task-capable action, `projects.execute`, returns `resultType:"task"`, and a client polls `tasks/get` through a project waiting on an approval, answers with `tasks/update` and reads a terminal result, with no Python service and no new table. O3 S15's capability aggregate is accepted and the project stays active: a card's run resolves its capability and executor, the capability's readiness is reported before the run starts, a cited passage comes from a pinned `strata` pack, and work-package memory is written, consolidated into `strata_rag` and recalled by `source_id`. O4 the tranche-7 exit gate exits 0 on three fresh receipts and hands a green tranche to the review that #755 records.

## Plan

Every member is one factory run, and the three packs are authored and preflighted as a set before the first write: `rework-batch.py` refuses to start a member whose pack has not passed the offline check, and it refuses the tranche outright while the demo cadence is missing. The factory executes the members in project-key order — S06c, S15, S16 — because `tranche_members` sorts by key; the WSJF ranking below is a value ordering, not the execution order, and the plan records both rather than implying the driver applies the ranking. S15 is the one member whose product is still moving: its slice lane (#9, PR #949) is open, so its pack is authored against the row as it settles and re-preflighted if that row changes.

## WSJF order

S16 — business value 9, time criticality 7, risk reduction 9, job size 8: (9+7+9)/8 = 3.13. S06c — 8, 6, 6, 8: 2.50. S15 — 10, 8, 7, 13: 1.92. The ranking is therefore S16, S06c, S15. The factory's execution order is S06c, S15, S16, which is the snapshot's key order and is what `tranche_members` sorts to; with three members and one snapshot for all three receipts, the difference changes which receipt lands first and nothing else, so the ranking is recorded for the review rather than enforced on the run. S15's job size is the largest because it carries five tables, a consolidation path and a partly unbuilt action surface.

## Capacity and WIP

Three members, one in flight at a time. The factory is serial by construction — `rework-batch.py` runs one project at a time and journals every transition, so an interrupted run resumes at the member it stopped on rather than re-running the tranche. WIP is one member plus the tranche's readiness set; the exit gate runs only after the third receipt is green and fresh at the same snapshot sha.

## Evidence

O1 is measured by `acceptance/programme/S16.toml` and the S16 receipt. O2 by `acceptance/programme/S06c.toml` and the S06c receipt. O3 by `acceptance/programme/S15.toml` and the S15 receipt. O4 by `scripts/check-tranche-exit.py --tranche 7`, which reads every member's latest receipt and exits 0 only when each one is green at the snapshot's head sha. The receipts land in `docs/evidence/rework/{S16,S06c,S15}.json`; the exit in `docs/evidence/rework/tranche-7/tranche-exit.json`.

## Dependencies

S16 depends on S02, S03, S04, S10 and S11, all of which are delivered and closed. S06c depends on S04, S05, S06 and S06b; S04 owns `/mcp`, S06b owns the licence principal and the tool list, and S06 owns the run and approval primitives. S15 depends on S13's `agent.run`, S10's copilot surface, S09's strata ingest and retrieval, S11's start seam, S03's catalogue and S16's prompt-audit provenance. No member of this tranche depends on a tranche that is not already closed.

## Backlog refinement

The re-estimate against the tranche-6 plan moves S15's job size from an unestimated backlog row to 13 on the strength of its five tables, the consolidation path and the seven actions step 5 still owes, and holds S16 at 8 and S06c at 8. The refinement reorders the membership from the seed's sequence (S06c, S15, S16) to the WSJF ranking S16, S06c, S15, with two reasons recorded: S16's product is fully in-tree and its receipt is the cheapest of the three to make green, and S15 is the only member whose product lane is still open. The reorder is recorded in the refinement cadence's meta and is read by the content preflight for the WSJF inputs; the factory's member order is the key sort, as the plan section above states.
